finding.claim: The user identity is taken directly from the client-supplied request header `X-Session-User-Verified`, with no session, signature or token check. Any caller can send the header with another user's name and pass every ACL check as that user. This lets them delete files (delete_file) and rename files (rename_file) they don't own. The header name suggests an upstream proxy sets it after verification. Nothing in this repository strips or overwrites a client-sent copy, so exploitability depends on a trusted proxy that is not visible here.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled HTTP request header `X-Session-User-Verified`, set to the victim or owner's username.
finding.sink: `del STORE[fid]` (views.py:18) and `f["name"] = request.json["name"]` (views.py:27), the protected delete and rename operations.

trace.note: before_request stores the raw header value in g.user with no verification
is_allowed checks `action in resource.grants.get(user, [])`, so a spoofed username inherits that user's grants
rename_file uses the same spoofable g.user for the write check
the rename is applied if the check passes

finding.guards_checked: Checked acl.py ensure_allowed/is_allowed. They only compare the username string against the grants. Checked views.py for any authentication decorator or header stripping. None exists, and the repo has only two files with no proxy or config. A missing header gives user None, which has no grants and is denied, so only a supplied header bypasses authorization.

verdict.guard_found: none in the repo. ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10) aborts 403 and is_allowed (acl.py:5) is tested at views.py:25. Both only compare the username string from the header against grants, so neither authenticates the caller. There is no header stripping, session check or signature check.
verdict.reason: views.py:11 copies the client-supplied X-Session-User-Verified header into g.user, and that value alone decides the ACL checks at views.py:17 and views.py:25 (acl.py:5), so any caller who knows an owner's name can delete or rename; the only caveat is that a trusted proxy outside the repo might strip the header, which can't be seen here.
